rule: H3-0 is the hypothesis as written: every Headroom-qualified cell, both conditions, all strata. Strata are a pre-registered heterogeneity analysis, not an admission rule. H3-R (RESPONSIVE only) is an additional hypothesis with its own estimand and cannot replace H3-0.

primary.question: Does forced release (A0 vs N0) have a net cost on recomputation, across the Headroom-qualified workload pool?
primary.population: every Headroom-qualified cell, both conditions, all strata
primary.flip_note: FLAT is INCLUDED. A small dRho measures A0's baseline sensitivity to pressure; it is not evidence about the arm-vs-A0 difference, so it cannot exclude a group from this hypothesis.
primary.estimator: group mean of Headroom-eligible cells, then mean / bootstrap over groups; one cell counts fully, two cells are averaged 1/2 each
primary.group_weight: 1 / group_count -- equal group weight, NOT proportional to cell count
primary.cell_weight_within_group: 1 / (cells in that group); 1 for a one-cell group

secondary_hypothesis.question: Is the forced-release cost observable in the subset whose baseline recomputation itself responds to pressure?
secondary_hypothesis.status: pre-registered, separate, not a replacement for H3-0
secondary_hypothesis.rationale: A non-trivial empirical marginal response ratio is a necessary condition for the mechanism to have anywhere to act. If the cost appears only here, that is a finding about the mechanism's domain; if it appears in H3-0 and not here, that is a finding about sensitivity, not a contradiction.
secondary_hypothesis.threshold_provenance: dRho >= 0.10, the same constant G4-a uses
secondary_hypothesis.estimator: group mean of Headroom-eligible cells, then mean / bootstrap over groups; one cell counts fully, two cells are averaged 1/2 each
secondary_hypothesis.group_weight: 1 / group_count -- equal group weight, NOT proportional to cell count
secondary_hypothesis.cell_weight_within_group: 1 / (cells in that group); 1 for a one-cell group

heterogeneity.status: pre-registered, descriptive, reported side by side
heterogeneity.note: No stratum gates another. The FLAT stratum is reported with its own interval even though its predicted effect is small, because 'predicted small' is not 'measured zero'.

WEAK.estimator: group mean of Headroom-eligible cells, then mean / bootstrap over groups; one cell counts fully, two cells are averaged 1/2 each
WEAK.group_weight: 1 / group_count -- equal group weight, NOT proportional to cell count
WEAK.cell_weight_within_group: 1 / (cells in that group); 1 for a one-cell group

FLAT.group_weight: 1 / group_count -- equal group weight, NOT proportional to cell count
FLAT.cell_weight_within_group: 1 / (cells in that group); 1 for a one-cell group

F.population: campaign runs all 20 groups, both conditions

A_PRIME.population: one measured operating point per group

E.population: one measured operating point per group

flat_policy: FLAT is retained in H3-0 and reported as its own heterogeneity stratum. It is not removed from the hypothesis; it is only expected to be uninformative, and expectation is not measurement.
